topic: The mistake of treating lead sourcing as part of your billable day.

hooks.text: Myth: Searching for business contacts counts as billable working time.

spec.headline: Mistake: Sourcing leads vs. billable work
spec.sub: Focus your billable hours on clients.

alts: Myth: Searching for business contacts counts as billable working time.

Slide 2 of 6: Looking up contact details is an administrative chore, not delivery.. When you spend your morning searching for local businesses to pitch, you use up your best energy on basic data entry. That time produces zero client output and earns nothing.

Slide 3 of 6: Treating setup tasks as productive work quietly caps your capacity.. Whether you offer video, bookkeeping, or consulting, your income depends on active outreach and actual client delivery. Sourcing contacts eats into the hours you should spend doing real work.

Slide 4 of 6: Separating setup tasks leaves your day open for pitching.. Treat contact gathering as raw preparation. When your contact list arrives ready in an Excel file, your work day starts directly with reaching out and talking to decision-makers.

Slide 5 of 6: Pre-qualified data puts relevant local businesses right in front of you.. We gather local business listings from Google Places and check their websites daily. You receive clean contact details, review counts, and active status so you can focus on outreach.
Slide 6 of 6: DM LEADS. If you sell services to local businesses and want a daily sheet of verified leads, send a message. We can discuss if this fits your current workflow.
